name: Cultural Marxism conspiracy theory
summary: A far-right narrative holding that a small group of Marxist critical theorists, above all the Frankfurt School, deliberately set out to destroy Western Christian civilisation by capturing cultural institutions and spreading 'political correctness', feminism, multiculturalism and sexual liberation. Its proponents call for resisting this culture war and restoring traditional Christian and Western cultural values; scholars find the theory without factual basis and see it as a recycling of the Nazi 'Cultural Bolshevism' trope.
scope: The contemporary 'Cultural Marxism' narrative as it arose in the US from the 1990s (Minnicino 1992, the Free Congress Foundation's Weyrich and Lind, Buchanan's The Death of the West) and its later alt-right and transnational uses, as described by scholarship (Jay, Paternotte and Verloo, Busbridge et al.) and by its proponents' own accounts (Lind's columns, Breshears's Brief History). It does not cover Marxist cultural analysis, the actual Frankfurt School or Gramscian cultural theory: Weiner's Cultural Marxism and Political Sociology (1981) is scholarship on that and is not tied to the conspiracy theory, and Bezmenov's Berserker Books volume (1988 title) names 'cultural Marxism' only in its title, so neither is used as a source.
